subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Should the WhatsApp plugin own a dedicated SQLite auth database, and what migration, rollback, backup, permissions, and external-`authDir` policy should govern existing linked accounts?
rationale: Upstream and repository policy support moving away from multi-file auth, but changing shipped credentials and cryptographic state requires explicit ownership and upgrade-safety decisions that automation cannot choose.

options.title: Dedicated Plugin SQLite
options.body: Create a dedicated WhatsApp auth database with typed serialization, atomic batches, explicit backup, and verified one-way migration.

options.title: Extend Shared Plugin State
options.body: Use the shared plugin-state store only after proving its size, binary serialization, transaction, backup, and lifecycle contracts meet Baileys requirements.

options.title: Retain Hardened Files
options.body: Keep multi-file auth and continue targeted atomicity and performance hardening if maintainers do not want to own the database migration now.

recommendation.title: Dedicated Plugin SQLite
recommendation.body: Create a dedicated WhatsApp auth database with typed serialization, atomic batches, explicit backup, and verified one-way migration.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the substantial recent auth persistence and recovery work spanning all central files.
